review.rationale: Replacing the temporal validity check (`row.valid_to is None or row.valid_to >= valid_at`) with `if True` eliminates the expiration filtering mechanism. This allows expired records (where `row.valid_to < valid_at`) to be processed as valid, producing an observable behavioral difference in the gateway's record evaluation.

review.label: NON_EQUIVALENT
review.rationale: The original condition `if row.valid_to is None or row.valid_to >= valid_at` filters rows based on temporal validity — a row is included only if it has no expiration date or its expiration date is on or after the reference date `valid_at`. Replacing this with `if True` unconditionally passes all rows regardless of their `valid_to` value. This means rows that have expired (where `row.valid_to < valid_at`) will now be included in the governed output that previously would have been excluded. This produces an observable behavioral difference: the set of rows returned or processed downstream will differ whenever any row exists with a non-null `valid_to` that is strictly less than `valid_at`.
